summary: @servicetitan/feature-spotlight preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package advertises itself as a React feature-spotlight UI styling helper, but ships a preinstall hook that turns `npm install` into an alternate-runtime dropper. `package.json` declares `scripts.preinstall: "node setup.mjs"`. `setup.mjs` downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<archive>.zip`, extracts and chmod+x's the `bun` binary, then `execFileSync`s it against `math_init.js` in the tarball root. `math_init.js` is a 711KB `// @bun @bun-cjs` compiled bundle with heavy identifier mangling, a large numeric/string constant table, and a rotating string-array decoder — a form the Node-based scanner cannot inspect, and which is not referenced from `dist/index.js` or the library's exports. The payload is executed only via the freshly downloaded Bun interpreter, evading Node-based static and runtime analysis. A React styling helper has no legitimate need to fetch a second language runtime and hand it a large opaque bundle at install time; the pattern (alternate-runtime + undeclared obfuscated payload + purpose mismatch + auto-execute preinstall) is a fetched-runtime dropper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
